summary: This lecture tells of the Prophet's journey to Taif after the deaths of Khadijah and Abu Talib. He walked about 90 km with Zaid ibn Harithah and met Taif's three leaders, Abd Yalil, Mas'ud and Habib, sons of Amr, who mocked and rejected him. They incited youths who pelted him until his feet stuck to his sandals with blood. He took refuge in the garden of Utba and Shayba, sons of Rabi'a, where their slave Adas from Nineveh embraced Islam after hearing Bismillah and the name of Prophet Yunus. After a long supplication Jibril came with the angels of the mountains, but the Prophet SAW refused to destroy Taif and hoped for future generations to believe. On the way back a group of jinn embraced Islam, and Mut'im ibn Adi escorted him back into Mecca.
keyPoints: The Prophet SAW walked about 90 km to Taif in secret with Zaid ibn Harithah to seek protection for his mission.
Taif's three leaders rejected and mocked him, then youths pelted him with stones until he bled.
Adas of Nineveh embraced Islam in Rabi'a's garden after hearing Bismillah and the name of Prophet Yunus.
The Prophet SAW refused the mountain angels' offer to destroy Taif because he was sent as a mercy.
Jinn embraced Islam on the way back, and Mut'im ibn Adi protected him into Mecca.

chapters.title: Opening: Taif and the stone-throwers
chapters.summary: The ustaz opens with the rejection by Taif's three leaders and the Prophet being pelted until blood stuck his feet to his sandals.

chapters.title: Recap of the year of sorrow
chapters.summary: The ustaz recaps losing Khadijah and Abu Talib and that Quraysh abuse worsened, such as filth placed on him in prostration.

chapters.title: The decision to leave for Taif
chapters.summary: He returned to an empty house, then left quietly with Zaid ibn Harithah on foot for Taif.

chapters.title: Taif and the three-day walk
chapters.summary: Taif is a cool highland with fruit and roses. The walk of about 90 km took at least three days.

chapters.title: Taif's three leaders
chapters.summary: The Prophet SAW met Abd Yalil, Mas'ud and Habib, sons of Amr, and delivered his message respectfully.

chapters.title: Rejection and mockery
chapters.summary: They mocked him. The Prophet SAW only asked them not to tell Mecca, but they stirred up the youths.

chapters.title: Pelted with stones
chapters.summary: Zaid tried to shield him but blood flowed until his sandals squelched. He recited Quran with his head bowed.

chapters.title: Rabi'a's garden
chapters.summary: He reached the garden of Rabi'a's sons Utba and Shayba, who sympathised as fellow Meccans and sent grapes through their slave.

chapters.title: Adas embraces Islam
chapters.summary: Adas heard Bismillah, learned the Prophet knew of Yunus of Nineveh, kissed him and embraced Islam.

chapters.title: The supplication at Taif
chapters.summary: He prayed, complaining of his weakness, saying that as long as Allah was not angry he would carry on.

chapters.title: The mountain angels
chapters.summary: Jibril came with two mountain angels offering to destroy Taif, but he refused, hoping for future generations.

chapters.title: Ibn Abbas and Taif today
chapters.summary: The ustaz notes Ibn Abbas taught thousands of students at Taif, because Taif was not destroyed.

chapters.title: Jinn embrace Islam
chapters.summary: On the way back, a group of jinn heard the Prophet SAW praying at night and embraced Islam.

chapters.title: Mut'im ibn Adi protects him
chapters.summary: Mut'im and his armed sons escorted him into Mecca for tawaf, without becoming Muslim.

chapters.title: Summary of three trials
chapters.summary: The ustaz sums up the post-boycott trials: being blamed, losing two pillars, and Taif. Masjid Adas still stands in Taif.

dalil.context: The ustaz says the Prophet was sent as a mercy to people, which is why he refused to destroy Taif.
dalil.translation: It was only as a mercy that We sent you [Prophet] to all people.

dalil.context: The ustaz tells of a group of jinn who heard the Prophet's Quran recitation in night prayer and believed.
dalil.translation: We sent a group of jinn to you [Prophet] to listen to the Quran. When they heard it, they said to one another, ‘Be quiet!’ Then when it was finished they turned to their community and gave them warning.
The Prophet SAW prayed: O Allah, to whom do You entrust me, a distant person who is harsh or a relative; as long as You are not angry with me, I do not mind.
dalil.context: The ustaz summarises this long supplication. He does not name a narrator or source.

dalil.translation: Jibril with two mountain angels offered to crush the people of Taif between two mountains, but the Prophet SAW hoped that from their descendants would come those who worship Allah.
dalil.context: The ustaz narrates this as the peak of his patience. He does not name a narrator or source.

dalil.translation: The Prophet SAW prayed for Ibn Abbas to be the most knowledgeable in Quran interpretation and fiqh.
dalil.context: The ustaz mentions this prayer while explaining Ibn Abbas teaching at Taif. He does not name a narrator or source.

people.context: Gifted by Khadijah to the Prophet, accompanied him to Taif and shielded him from stones with his hands and face.
One of the three brothers who mocked him.
Sneered that he would not speak with someone so exalted.
Called him a liar and a deceiver.

people.role: Owner of a garden in Taif
people.context: Sympathised as fellow Meccans and sent grapes to him through Adas.
Startled by Bismillah and the name of Yunus, he kissed the Prophet SAW and embraced Islam.
Mentioned by the Prophet SAW to Adas as proof that he too was a prophet.
Came with two mountain angels after his supplication at Taif.
Prayed for by him and later taught thousands of students at Taif.
Escorted him with his armed sons into Mecca.
Asked Mut'im whether he had become Muslim or was only offering protection.

sirah.summary: This lecture covers the journey to Taif, the rejected mission, Adas, the mountain angels, the jinn and Mut'im's protection.

lessons.title: Mercy toward those who harm
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW refused to destroy Taif and hoped their descendants would believe, a hope realised through Ibn Abbas.

lessons.title: Carry on as long as Allah is not angry
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW prayed that as long as Allah was not angry, he would continue.

lessons.title: Etiquette when visiting
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW went to the local leaders, asked permission and spoke courteously.

lessons.title: Allah sends relief after trials
lessons.body: After the stoning, Allah gave him Adas and the believing jinn.

lessons.title: The name of Allah opens hearts
lessons.body: Adas embraced Islam after hearing only Bismillah.

lessons.title: Valuing protectors even if not Muslim
lessons.body: Mut'im protected him without becoming Muslim, and his help was not forgotten.

lessons.title: Do not seek dealings with jinn
lessons.body: We need not preach to jinn or deal with them; it is not our concern.

lessons.title: Rising after loss
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW kept striving despite being blamed and losing two pillars.

lessons.title: Loyalty to adopted son and companions
lessons.body: Zaid risked himself shielding him from stones.

glossary.meaning: A cool highland town of fruit and roses, a retreat for Meccans.
A servant bound to a master, like Adas in the garden.
A city in Iraq, home of Prophet Yunus.
Angels in charge of the mountains who offered to destroy Taif.
Beings of another realm, some obedient and some becoming devils.
A guarantee of safety from a protector, like Mut'im.
A mosque in Taif at the site of that garden.

children.detail: As long as Allah is not angry.
